newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Costello backs Morgan position on RBA board.
newsitem.headline: Costello backs Morgan position on RBA board.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Wednesday lent support to Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) director Hugh Morgan after media speculation of a conflict of interest in the bank's move to sell down gold reserves.
"I believe that Mr Morgan makes a strong contribution to the activities of the bank and I look forward to him continuing to do so," Costello said.

The RBA announced on July 4 it had sold 167 tonnes of gold, or two-thirds of its reserves over the previous six months. This news contributed to a fall in the gold price to 12 year lows on world markets.
Morgan is also managing director of WMC Ltd, a company that has forward sales of more than three million ounces of gold to hedge against a weak gold price.
Last week Morgan issued a statement denying any impropriety which was shortly followed by a statement from RBA governor, Ian MacFarlane, backing Morgan.
Costello said WMC's forward gold sales were declared to the market and he was not concerned about the conduct of the board.
"I think Western Mining's (WMC) forward sales in relation to gold were publicly reported right throughout last year and into this year," Costello said.
Costello also rejected calls for minutes of RBA meetings to be released publicly and said the RBA's current system of disclosure was more than adequate.
"The Reserve Bank comes out, announces its decisions and publishes them. You can't get any better than that," Costello said. "It is quite independent in the discharge of its activities."
